articles.summary:
Alternative ways being used to move fuel out of Gulf region, but flows of refined products such as diesel still constrained

Exports of crude from the strait of Hormuz have largely returned to levels seen before the outbreak of the Iran war, as oil producers and the shipping industry have found alternative ways of transporting crucial fuel out of the Middle East.

Pipeline exports and ship-to-ship transfers are among the methods being used, according to analysts tracking the situation, while the US military continues to escort some vessels. However, flows of refined products such as diesel remain constrained, pushing prices higher.

The spokesperson said the attacks - which targeted Houthi movements, reinforcements, gatherings, personnel, vehicles and military equipment - inflicted losses on the group.

articles.title: US arrests Energy Department employee under claims of backing Yemen’s Houthis
articles.summary:
US arrests Energy Department employee under claims of backing Yemen’s Houthis

The Justice Department has arrested a man under claims that he attempted to provide material support or resources to Yemen’s Houthis.

The 51 year-old, identified as Ashton Hamed Ellaboudy, is a US Energy Department employee. 

"As alleged, a US government employee travelled overseas and used his specialised expertise in an attempt to aid the Houthis, a designated Foreign Terrorist Organization backed by Iran," the assistant attorney general for national security, John A Eisenberg, said. 

Eisenberg claimed that Ellaboudy "acquired materials for the construction of explosive material and drones capable of delivering these explosives".

"These allegations are so deeply disturbing that they almost defy imagination," he added.

Ellaboudy is scheduled to appear before a federal judge on 2 October in Washington.

articles.title: No Iranian oil exports in September: Bessent
articles.summary:
No Iranian oil exports in September: Bessent

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has claimed in a post on X that “Iran loaded ZERO crude oil onto tankers in September”.

The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April in an attempt to thwart Iranian exports, the most profitable of which is oil sold principally to China. 

The blockade, which Bessent claimed is severing Tehran "economic lifeline", has deepened Iran's inflation crisis, but had also long been blighted by reports of ships passing through it in spite of US efforts to contain them. 

Iran loaded ZERO crude oil onto tankers in September. The Trump Administration is cutting off the Iranian regime’s most critical source of revenue.

Houthi-run media meanwhile reported incoming attacks in the cities of Sanaa, Taiz, Saada and Amran.

articles.title: Eritrea and Ethiopia shutter embassies as new Red Sea conflict looms
articles.summary:
Eritrea and Ethiopia shutter embassies as new Red Sea conflict looms

Submitted by Sean Mathews on Thu, 10/01/2026 - 19:22
In response to Ethiopia's embassy closure, Eritrea accused Addis Ababa of funding armed groups to topple government
Tigray People's Liberation Front fighters walk towards a field in Mekele, the capital of the Tigray region, Ethiopia, on 30 June 2021(Yasuyoshi Chiba/AFP)
Off

Eritrea and Ethiopia have severed all diplomatic ties after accusing one another of engaging in hostile actions, in a major flare-up that could foreshadow another war on the volatile Red Sea.

Ethiopia on Thursday announced it was expelling 10 Eritrean diplomats and closing its embassy in Eritrea’s capital of Asmara, after reports of explosions in Addis Ababa.

The strike punctured Addis Ababa’s relative calm despite Ethiopia’s federal government battling an alliance of rebel movements opposed to Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed in Ethiopia’s regions of Tigray, Amhara and Afar.

Western and regional officials in Addis Ababa confirmed to Middle East Eye the sound of explosions in the capital due to a drone strike. AFP reported that the explosion rocked the Ethiopian National Defence Force headquarters in the Tor Hayloch area of Addis Ababa. 

In a statement, Ethiopia accused Eritrea of engaging in “direct and indirect acts of hostility and belligerence” against it.

Eritrea said in response it was severing all diplomatic relations with Ethiopia, accusing it of pursuing “an agenda of incessant hostility” against it. 

“In parallel with these aggressive intentions, Ethiopia has gone further to host, train, and provide arms to an assortment of what it calls ‘Eritrean armed opposition groups’ to stoke internal conflict for ‘regime change’ in Eritrea,” Eritrea’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement.

Deterioration of ties, risks

Eritrea and Ethiopia have been at odds for months, with regional diplomats warning that ties were deteriorating fast.

The two briefly formed an alliance to fight the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), the ruling party in Ethiopia's Tigray region, during Ethiopia’s 2020-2022 civil war. Since then, they have returned to being bitter foes.

Addis Ababa has made claims against Eritrea’s Red Sea coastline and accuses Eritrea of supporting rebel groups like the TPLF, which Asmara denies.

"[Abiy Ahmed] has a two-waters strategy like Israel. Only for him it is from the Nile River to the Red Sea," Eritrean Foreign Minister Osman Saleh told MEE in an exclusive interview from Asmara last month. He referred to an Israeli expansionist vision that stretches from the Gaza Strip to the Jordan River at the frontier of the occupied West Bank. 

Exclusive: UAE pursuing 'port imperialism' across Africa, Eritrean foreign minister says
Read More »

With fighting already flaring between Ethiopia’s federal government and the TPLF, a breakdown in relations with Eritrea could widen the war to the Red Sea at a time when Yemen and Sudan are both in conflict.

The risk is that the conflict could draw in regional players, including Egypt, Turkey, Somalia, and the Gulf states.

The TPLF is already aligned with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), which are fighting the Rapid Support Forces, a militia accused of genocide that is backed by the UAE and has training camps in Ethiopia. Eritrea is aligned with Egypt and Saudi Arabia in supporting the SAF.

One of Ethiopia’s staunchest supporters is the UAE, which has provided drones and other military supplies to Abiy Ahmed’s forces.

Saleh also told MEE that Asmara believes the UAE is cooperating with Israel against Asmara.

Israel has a historical precedent for supporting Ethiopia. In the late 1970s and late 1980s, Israel provided arms to Ethiopia's Marxist Derg government, which were used against Eritrean fighters.

articles.title: Oil supertanker hit in Hormuz: Iranian media
articles.summary:
Oil supertanker hit in Hormuz: Iranian media

An oil supertanker is in flames in the Strait of Hormuz after it was hit by a missile, Iran’s Fars news agency is reporting. 

The attack took place eight kilometres off the coast of Oman, Fars reported, without attributing a perpetrator to the attack. 

The attack is the latest in a spate of attacks on vessels in the strait, with UK Maritime Trade Operations logging three incidents on Wednesday alone. US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the strait on Sunday.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia conducting joint investigation into Flydubai incident with UAE
articles.summary:
Saudi Arabia conducting joint investigation into Flydubai incident with UAE

Saudi Arabia has said that it is conducting a joint investigation with the UAE into the Emirati Flydubai plane that made an emergency landing on its territory on Wednesday after a mid-flight incident between its pilots. 

The Saudi interior ministry added in a statement that its initial probe indicates that the co-pilot on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv had assaulted the captain, consistent with earlier reporting. 

Relations between Riyadh and Abu Dhabi worsened dramatically this year over the UAE's support for secessionist movements in Yemen, Sudan, Libya and Somalia. But in recent months, the two states have signalled signs of rapprochement amid a renewed offensive from their mutual enemy, the Houthi rebel group in Yemen.

articles.title: Turkey echoes denial of Syria-Hezbollah meeting on its turf
articles.summary:
Turkey echoes denial of Syria-Hezbollah meeting on its turf

Turkey has denied a Reuters report alleging that a secretive meeting between representatives of Syria and Hezbollah took place on Turkish soil last month. 

Turkey's Directorate of Communications said that the report, which cited six sources briefed on the matter, is "entirely unfounded". 

Syria has also denied that the meeting took place, as covered on Middle East Eye's live blog earlier on Thursday.

Saudi Arabia is renewing its alliance with the UAE and launching extensive military operations, while the G7 and the UK step up diplomatic pressure against Iranian support for the rebels.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování vojenských operací v Jemenu, nárůst diplomatické aktivity mezi Saúdskou Arábií a UAE a zvýšenou volatilitu cen komodit.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, military operations in Yemen, increased diplomatic activity between Saudi Arabia and the UAE, and heightened commodity price volatility are expected to continue.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Rudého moře a úžiny Bab al-Mandab zůstává extrémně napjatá kvůli eskalaci bojů mezi Houthii a provládními silami v Jemenu. Omezená průplavnost klíčových námořních koridorů a přetrvávající hrozby pro globální energetickou infrastrukturu nadále drží trhy v pohotovosti.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait remains extremely tense due to escalating fighting between the Houthis and pro-government forces in Yemen. Limited transit through key maritime corridors and ongoing threats to global energy infrastructure continue to keep markets on high alert.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování intenzivních bojů v Jemenu, nárůst tlaku na diplomatické řešení ze strany G7 a přetrvávající volatilitu cen ropy kvůli bezpečnostním rizikům v námořních koridorech.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, intensive fighting in Yemen, increased pressure for a diplomatic resolution from the G7, and persistent oil price volatility due to security risks in maritime corridors are expected to continue.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v Rudém moři a oblasti Bab al-Mandab zůstává vysoce napjatá navzdory postupnému návratu části ropných toků a plánům kontejnerových aliancí na návrat k trasám přes Suez. Útoky neznámých projektilů na tankery v Hormuzském průlivu a eskalace pozemních bojů v Jemenu nicméně nadále udržují vysokou prémii za geopolitické riziko v klíčových námořních koridorech.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab region remains highly tense despite the gradual return of some oil flows and container alliances planning to resume Suez routes. However, attacks by unknown projectiles on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and escalating ground fighting in Yemen continue to sustain a high geopolitical risk premium in key maritime corridors.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování potyček v oblasti Rudého moře a Hormuzského průlivu, přičemž trhy budou nadále citlivě reagovat na jakékoliv zprávy o obnovení plného provozu přes Suez.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, skirmishes in the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz are expected to continue, with markets remaining highly sensitive to any news regarding the full resumption of traffic through Suez.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v Rudém moři a okolí zůstává kritická kvůli eskalaci bojů mezi Houthi a saúdsky podporovanými silami. Navíc dochází k přímým útokům na ropné tankery v Hormuzském průlivu a diplomatické roztržce mezi Etiopií a Eritreou.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Red Sea and surrounding regions remains critical due to escalating fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed forces. Furthermore, direct attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and a diplomatic rift between Ethiopia and Eritrea compound regional instability.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování vojenských operací v Jemenu a zvýšené napětí v Hormuzském průlivu, přičemž trhy budou nadále opatrně testovat alternativní námořní trasy.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, military operations in Yemen and heightened tensions in the Strait of Hormuz are expected to continue, while markets cautiously test alternative maritime routes.
